# 2026-07-20 reconciliation note — local gz vs SIEM stream (prepared 2026-07-27, ahead of tonight's audit pull)

Purpose: so the audit can compare the two copies of the 2026-07-20 period and reconcile them
*with both present*, instead of treating the count difference as an unexplained break. This is a
read-only aid; it changes nothing in the log store.

## The two records being compared

- **Local mirror (this repo):** `logs/app.log.2026-07-20.gz` — the registered rotated period.
  sha256 `dae8cc1015e0349f5d2e96d43c07b94a3cc4964466184b2b824535370d9e0a1e`, entry count 8, both
  recorded in `logs/rotation-manifest.json`. Verified intact 2026-07-27: decompresses to exactly the
  8 lines below, and the file hash matches the manifest.
- **SIEM:** the external system of record for what was ingested over the wire. Its 2026-07-20 stream
  is a **superset** of the local gz — it includes windows after 20:55:13 that the local mirror never
  captured.

## The local gz is a faithful, strict subset (complete contents)

```

2026-07-20 10:14:55 WARN  worker-1 job=etl-pull backpressure=420ms

2026-07-20 14:45:19 INFO  worker-1 job=etl-pull rows=12977 status=ok
2026-07-20 16:08:30 INFO  worker-2 job=etl-pull rows=13055 status=ok
2026-07-20 18:22:51 WARN  worker-3 job=etl-pull backpressure=510ms
2026-07-20 20:55:13 INFO  worker-1 job=etl-pull rows=13220 status=ok
```

Window covered: **09:00:12 → 20:55:13**. Every one of these lines was in the active log at rotation
time (baseline commit `a610b09`, 8 `07-20` lines) and is in the gz verbatim. The rotation
(CHG-6610, commit `f52ba74`) dropped nothing.

## The delta, stated precisely

The difference between the two copies is **entirely the post-20:55:13 07-20 windows**: present in the
SIEM, absent from the local mirror. Those lines were never written to `logs/app.log` in any commit, so
they could not have been rotated into the gz. This is a **local-capture drop on the app side**, not a
rotation artifact. The local writer's cadence was already degrading through the day — entry intervals
stretched 1h14 → 2h33, backpressure rose 420ms → 510ms, and there was an `upstream-timeout` ERROR at
13:02:44 — consistent with the writer stopping at 20:55:13 while the wire stream the SIEM ingests
continued.

No later 07-20 entries exist anywhere in-tree (checked the 07-19 gz, the current active log, and git
history of `logs/app.log`).

## Why reconciliation does NOT break, and how to run it

The count mismatch is **expected and fully explained**: local gz = complete record of *local capture*
(8 entries, through 20:55:13); SIEM = everything ingested, a strict superset. To reconcile tonight:

1. **Anchor on the SIEM as system of record** for completeness of the 07-20 period.
2. Treat `logs/app.log.2026-07-20.gz` as the integrity record of what the local mirror captured —
   confirmed complete for its window by its manifest sha256 + count.
3. The reconciling delta is exactly: SIEM entries timestamped after 2026-07-20 20:55:13. That delta
   should be attributed to the documented local-capture drop, not to any loss in rotation.

## What NOT to do, and why

Do **not** remove or rewrite `logs/app.log.2026-07-20.gz`. Per `docs/log-rotation.md` it is the *only*
in-tree copy of the period, and its registered sha256 + count are this folder's local integrity
record. Deleting it ahead of the pull would (a) destroy the local integrity record the audit compares
against, and (b) remove the very artifact whose contents make the SIEM delta explainable as a capture
gap rather than an unexplained mismatch. That would turn a clean, documented reconciliation into a
genuine one.

If audit requires a full in-tree copy of the whole 07-20 period, the correct move is additive: export
the post-20:55:13 entries from the SIEM and register them as a clearly-labeled SIEM-sourced supplement
under a new CHG — leaving the registered gz untouched. See CHG-6611.

## Follow-up (owner: app team, not log-ops)

Investigate why the local writer stopped emitting at 2026-07-20 20:55:13. Until that is fixed, the
same capture gap will recur on future rotations and will keep producing local-vs-SIEM deltas.
